correctness.rationale: Each mixed rough vertex is exactly a cut-edge endpoint. A rooted tree integrates every edge-subset as exactly two complementary 0/1 colorings. Hence central inverses are precisely twice the edge covers, with full cut-size polynomial equality. For every other realized observation Q, the mixed set is proper and observed colors outside the mixed set fix the global orientation; each cut F is inside T[S] and covers S. Completing it by the fixed set of all edges outside E(T[S]) covers V, shifts degree by h>=1 and is injective on the fiber. Thus coefficientwise dominance and strict unique maximum follow for all n>=2, and the uniform-output min-entropy formula is immediate. Rooted two-state subtree recurrence uses exact conditioning on the parent edge. The package checker independently enumerated all labeled trees on 2..7 vertices (18,248 total), 1,462,212 realized rough fibers and 600 seeded larger trees. These experiments are finite corroboration, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: For any finite tree, the maximum inverse image under a natural paired lower/upper rough observation exactly quantifies the most information lost. The full coefficientwise injection over every alternative observation is a structural inequality, not merely a path count or textbook graph invariant. The resulting unique maximizer, factor-of-two separation, min-entropy formula and linear-arithmetic recursion apply to all branching patterns and provide a reusable benchmark for loss of information under rough observation. No paper-sized application is assumed; the precise invariant is naturally motivated by inverse-map ambiguity.
